correctness.rationale: The published class has unique p (the only prime at odd exponent), so no multiplicity overcount. Terms exponent>=5 satisfy sum_{p,j>=1}sqrt(X/p^(4j+1))=O(sqrt(X)) by convergent p^-5/2 series. In the e=1 layer dropping p∤k adds only O(sqrt X) pairs by k=p*l, sum_p sqrt(X/p^3). The main sum M(X)=sum_{odd k<=sqrt(X/3)} pi(X/k^2;8,3). For fixed k the progression PNT yields (log X/X)*pi(X/k^2;8,3)->1/(4k^2). Split k<=X^(1/4): Chebyshev bound pi(y)<<y/log y gives uniform C/k^2 bound since y>=sqrt X; k>X^(1/4): pi(y)<=y yields O(log X*X^(-1/4)). Dominated convergence gives 1/4 sum_odd k^-2=(1/4)(pi^2/8)=pi^2/32. Error O(sqrt X) is o(X/log X). Independent exact prime/square enumeration at X=200000 gave 6160 members (11 in e>=5 layers); finite counts are not proof of the asymptotic.
